name: The Messthetics
label: Dischord
lede: Fugazi's rhythm section found a jazz guitarist from D.C., played one show with him for [[Ian MacKaye]] and walked out with a Dischord deal. Eight years later they were on the label that put out A Love Supreme.

eras.title: Rome, a guitarist and a first show
eras.text: Joe Lally and Brendan Canty spent sixteen years locked together in Fugazi. Afterward Canty scored films and TV, and Lally moved his family to Rome. Back home, Lally and Canty started playing again, and Anthony Pirog came in from the jazz side.

years.h: Back from Rome, Lally plays Canty his solo recordings
years.p: Canty hears the tapes and suggests a guitarist he admires: Pirog, a D.C. player from the jazz and experimental side of town.
years.xp: Lally had been living in Rome. Canty had joined Fugazi in 1987, a year after Lally, and the two had not stopped being a rhythm section in anyone's mind. Per Wikipedia, the guitarist Canty named was someone he had long admired.

years.cap: The Messthetics at The Anthem, Washington, D.C., October 8, 2017
years.h: A backing band for a Zorn project walks out with a Dischord deal
years.p: Pirog asks Lally and Canty to be his rhythm section on a record for [[John Zorn|7ec4a553-73e5-4c0d-a071-a82b83a309e6]]'s Tzadik label. At their first show, [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] makes them another offer.
years.xp:
MacKaye had stood beside Lally and Canty on stage for sixteen years in Fugazi, and he was at the first show. Per Wikipedia, he liked what he heard enough to offer the trio a spot on Dischord, and the Tzadik record never happened.

For Canty it closed a loop: his first Dischord releases were with [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] in the mid-'80s. Pirog, by contrast, came from jazz and experimental labels.

eras.title: Two hundred shows, no singer
eras.text: An instrumental band made of a punk rhythm section and a jazz guitarist had no obvious audience. The Messthetics went and found one by touring, the way Fugazi did, and the second album, Anthropocosmic Nest, came out of it.

years.cap: Joe Lally and Brendan Canty at the Black Cat, Washington, D.C., June 8, 2018
years.p: Nine songs recorded through 2017 in Canty's practice space, mostly live, with no vocals and few overdubs. Critics reached for "jazz punk jam."
years.xp: Dischord's own description: nine songs recorded at Canty's studio space throughout 2017. The LP went out on clear vinyl and runs from Mythomania to The Weaver.

years.cap: The Messthetics at the Black Cat Mainstage, Washington, D.C., June 8, 2018
years.h: More than 200 shows in a year, and nobody sings
years.p: Dischord counts the year after the debut at upwards of 200 shows across the U.S., Europe and Asia. Two Fugazi veterans are back in vans.
years.xp: Dischord's bio puts the run in the year after the 2018 debut. A June 2018 show at the Black Cat in Washington is pictured here, and NPR filmed the trio for a Tiny Desk concert that same month.

yt: Record release show, Black Cat, D.C. (fan-shot)
years.h: Anthropocosmic Nest follows two years on the road
years.p: Eleven tracks from the practice space, from Better Wings to Touch Earth Touch Sky, recorded through 2019 to catch the live band. Dischord No. 189.
years.xp:
Dischord says the record comes from "a more experienced band, whose dialog as a performing unit had necessarily focused and intensified." Canty mixed it, [[TJ Lipple|ed4cd729-b4d2-4016-a0b6-c362b68d2afb]] mastered it, and it came out September 6, 2019.

Bandcamp put it on its Best Punk list for September 2019. The release show was at the Black Cat in D.C.

eras.title: Impulse!, and a tenor saxophone
eras.text: The Messthetics put out their next two records on Impulse! Records, the jazz label behind A Love Supreme, with tenor saxophonist James Brandon Lewis out front. Dischord distributes the first.

years.cap: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis at the INNtöne festival, July 18, 2025
q: It's like a well-oiled machine playing with them.
years.h: The label that put out A Love Supreme releases a Messthetics record
years.p: Nine tracks with saxophonist James Brandon Lewis, cut at Tonal Park in D.C. with producer Don Godwin, from L'Orso to Fourth Wall. Stereogum made it album of the week and Spin gave it an A−.
years.xp:
Lewis and the band are credited as producers alongside Godwin, and the album runs 46 minutes and 17 seconds. Spin heard "volatile chemistry" in the rhythm section; the Washington Post said Lewis's saxophone "adds a bold voice to what the trio has done previously."

Dischord sells the album in its store as a distributed release.

years.h: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis, "Emergence"
yt: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis, "Emergence"

years.cap: Anthony Pirog at the INNtöne festival, July 18, 2025
years.src: Bandcamp: Deface the Currency · 102.9 The Buzz
years.h: Eight years on, the band takes another run at Serpent Tongue
years.p: Deface the Currency, the second Impulse! album with Lewis, was announced in January 2026 with a tour. It has seven tracks.
years.xp: It closes on Serpent Tongue (Slight Return), a new take on the song from the band's 2018 Dischord debut. The album came out February 20.
